title: Tiramisù
intro: Coffee-soaked ladyfingers and mascarpone cream: Italy's favourite spoon dessert.

steps.t: Make the coffee and let it cool in a shallow bowl.
Separate the eggs: use very fresh ones, as they stay raw. Whisk the yolks with the sugar until pale and foamy.
Add the mascarpone to the yolks a spoonful at a time, stirring until the cream is smooth.
Whisk the whites with the salt to stiff peaks and fold them gently into the cream.
Dip the ladyfingers quickly in the coffee, one at a time, and make a layer in a 20×30 cm dish.
Cover with half the cream, add another layer of dipped ladyfingers and finish with the rest of the cream.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, so it sets.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Just before serving, dust generously with sifted cocoa.

tips.t: One second per side in the coffee is enough: soggy ladyfingers make it watery.
A spoonful of Marsala in the coffee gives it that Italian restaurant flavour.
Covered in the fridge, eat it within 2 days, since the eggs are raw.

title: Panna cotta with berries
intro: Vanilla cream just set, soft and wobbly, with a mixed berry sauce.

steps.t: Soak the gelatine sheets in cold water.
steps.label: Gelatine

steps.t: Meanwhile heat cream, milk, sugar, vanilla seeds and pod until just below the boil.
Take off the heat, remove the pod and stir in the squeezed-out gelatine until dissolved.
Pour the cream into 6 moulds or glasses.
Chill for at least 4 hours, until set but still wobbly.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Cook the berries with the sugar over medium heat until they break down into a sauce.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Dip the moulds in hot water for 5 seconds, turn them out onto plates and spoon over the cold sauce.

tips.t: For a vegetarian version use 2 g agar instead of gelatine and boil it in the cream for 1 minute.
Instead of the berry sauce, try a drizzle of caramel or melted dark chocolate.

title: Crème brûlée
intro: Vanilla custard baked in a water bath under a crust of caramelised sugar.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 150 °C.
Heat the cream with the split vanilla pod and seeds until just below the boil, then turn off the heat.
Leave it to infuse, then remove the pod.
steps.label: Infuse

steps.t: Whisk the yolks with the sugar without beating in air, then slowly pour in the hot cream, stirring.
Strain, skim off the foam and pour into 6 shallow ramekins set in a tray with hot water halfway up.
Bake until the edges are set and the centre barely wobbles.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let them cool, then chill for at least 3 hours.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Sprinkle each with a tablespoon of brown sugar and caramelise it with a blowtorch until amber.

tips.t: No blowtorch? Put the ramekins under the grill on full, very close, for 2 minutes.
Instead of vanilla, infuse the cream with 4 crushed cardamom pods or a strip of orange zest.

title: Chocolate mousse
intro: Just dark chocolate, eggs and a little sugar: light and intense.

steps.t: Melt the chocolate over simmering water, take it off the heat and let it cool until lukewarm.
Separate the eggs, very fresh since they stay raw. Stir the yolks into the chocolate one at a time until thick and glossy.
Whisk the whites with the salt; once foamy add the sugar and whisk to stiff, glossy peaks.
Stir a third of the whites firmly into the chocolate to loosen it.
Fold in the rest gently, lifting from the bottom, until no white streaks remain.
Spoon the mousse into 6 small bowls or one serving dish.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours, until set.
steps.label: Chill

tips.t: Use the chocolate lukewarm: hot, it cooks the yolks; cold, it seizes with the whites.
A pinch of flaky salt or chilli on top brings out the cocoa.
Serve with a few raspberries and a spoonful of unsweetened whipped cream.

title: Crema catalana
intro: Milk custard with lemon and cinnamon under a crust of burnt sugar.

steps.t: Heat the milk with strips of lemon peel and the cinnamon until just below the boil.
Turn off the heat, let it infuse, then strain the milk.
steps.label: Infuse

steps.t: Whisk yolks, sugar and cornstarch, pour in the milk slowly, stirring, and return it all to the pan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens and the first bubble appears; take off the heat at once.
steps.label: Custard

steps.t: Pour into shallow terracotta dishes and let it cool.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Just before serving, sprinkle with sugar and burn it with a blowtorch until amber and crisp.

tips.t: Burn the sugar at the last minute: the crust only stays crisp for a few minutes.
In Catalonia it is eaten on Saint Joseph's Day, 19 March: serve it with a small glass of moscatel.

title: Chocolate pudding
intro: Old-fashioned homemade pudding: milk, cocoa and chocolate, no packet mix.

steps.t: In a small saucepan whisk together sugar, cocoa, cornstarch and salt.
Pour in the cold milk slowly, whisking, until there are no lumps.
Bring to the boil over medium heat, stirring constantly, then cook 2 minutes until thick like custard.
steps.label: Cook

steps.t: Take off the heat and stir in the chopped chocolate until melted.
Pour into a mould rinsed with cold water and left wet, or into 4 small bowls.
Let it cool, cover and chill until firm.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Turn the pudding out onto a plate, or serve it in the bowls.

tips.t: Made with oat or soy milk and dairy-free chocolate it becomes a vegan pudding.
Serve it with a dollop of whipped cream and chopped toasted hazelnuts.

title: Kheer
intro: Indian rice pudding: slowly reduced milk, cardamom, saffron and pistachios.

steps.t: Rinse the rice several times and leave it to soak in cold water.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Meanwhile bring the milk to the boil in a heavy-based pan.
Add the drained rice and the crushed cardamom seeds, then turn the heat right down.
Simmer, stirring often and scraping the bottom, until the rice breaks down and the milk has reduced and thickened.
steps.label: Kheer

steps.t: Add sugar, saffron and raisins and cook a few minutes more.
steps.label: Sugar

steps.t: Turn off the heat: it thickens as it cools. Serve warm or cold, topped with chopped pistachios and almonds.

tips.t: A teaspoon of rose water stirred in at the end gives it the scent of Diwali sweets.
It thickens a lot when cold: loosen it with a splash of milk before serving.
